first.rationale: Both presenting symptoms (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) sit on the same funnel segment, and onboarding is upstream of activation, so one well-scoped onboarding experiment can plausibly move both. memory_86 is the closest prior: shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve, with a known, excludable harm in complex-workspace accounts. memory_31 corroborates that friction reduction lifts SMB activation. I want the memory_86 source record because the inherited summary tells me the direction of the complex-workspace churn effect but not its magnitude, the segment definition used, or whether the adoption lift persisted past the early window — all of which determine whether exclusion is a sufficient guard or whether the harm bled into adjacent segments. I want the memory_91 source record because activation messaging is the obvious alternative for the larger 6% drop, but its recorded outcome is entirely proxy (week-one engagement, first meaningful action) with no retention or revenue endpoint; if the archive shows a downstream revenue read, it may outrank onboarding and I would switch. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records acquisition and revenue lift but a material 30-day retention hit, which is directly adverse to the sustainable-long-term-qualified-revenue objective — it would buy the quarter and sell the year. referral_incentive is the safest memory on record but targets established customers and addresses neither presenting decline. enterprise_sales_assist is off-segment for an SMB-driven problem. Key uncertainty I am not resolving away: every candidate memory here is scored on funnel proxies (completion, activation, engagement), not on retained qualified revenue, so a completion-rate win is not yet evidence of a value win. I will therefore instrument the experiment on 30/60-day retention and qualified revenue as primary endpoints with completion as a secondary diagnostic, hold out complex-workspace accounts entirely per memory_86, and keep a kill criterion on early churn. If memory_86's archived record shows the complex-workspace harm was larger than summarized or the segment boundary was fuzzy, I will downscale to a small guarded test rather than proceed at standard scale.

final.rationale: I am switching from my provisional onboarding pick to activation_messaging, and both archive pulls are the reason. exp_91 resolved exactly the uncertainty I flagged: it is not a proxy-only result. It carries activation +6% AND 30-day retention +1%, meaning the engagement lift converted into retained accounts rather than borrowed motion. That is the only candidate on record with a measured downstream endpoint and no recorded harm, which is the profile the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective asks for. It also maps onto the larger of the two presenting declines: activation is down 6% QoQ and exp_91 recovered +6% activation. exp_86 moved the other way once I saw the source. The inherited summary said 'raised early churn'; the record says 60-day churn +9% in complex-workspace accounts. That harm is both larger and later-horizon than the summary conveyed, and a 60-day effect is harder to catch with a kill criterion inside a one-week slot. The +13% completion is real and the exclusion guard is real, but the compressed memory understated the downside, which is precisely the case for de-rating it rather than trusting the summary. I still consider simplify_onboarding a live future candidate, but it needs a clean complex-workspace segment definition before it runs, and I do not have budget to establish that now. promotional_pricing remains rejected despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 pairs its revenue lift with a material 30-day retention hit, so it trades long-term qualified revenue for a quarter of acquisition, which inverts the objective. The competitor pressure creates real urgency to do something price-shaped, and I am explicitly declining to let that urgency override the recorded retention harm. referral_incentive is safe but off-target for an SMB funnel decline; enterprise_sales_assist is off-segment. Uncertainty I am carrying forward rather than resolving away: exp_91 was run in a pre-competitor environment, so its +6% activation was measured against a baseline that was not being actively poached, and the effect may attenuate now. The +1% retention is small enough that I should not treat it as a confirmed value win, only as evidence of no harm. And this experiment does nothing for onboarding completion at -4%, which remains an open problem. I will run at standard scale with 30/60-day retention and qualified revenue as primary endpoints, activation as secondary diagnostic, and I will read the complex-workspace cohort separately so this experiment also generates the segment definition that simplify_onboarding needs before it can be safely scheduled.
